minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard a strong FY21 closeout and approved its revised procedures and goals document.
minutes.summary: The finance director reported FY21 revenues above estimates, appropriation closeouts and higher estimated free cash. Members asked whether the town is effectively budgeting to create free cash. The fire chief and the council on aging director briefed the committee ahead of budget season. The committee approved the amended procedures and goals document and the August 12 minutes, then heard reports on TC Passios, Marshall Park septic work and a school transfer.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted unanimously to approve its amended goals and procedures document.
The finance director reported FY21 revenues above estimates, mostly from local receipts, and estimated free cash above last year's certified amount.
Group health insurance closed out under budget, mostly from planned hires not made, and investment interest fell sharply, so the FY22 estimate may need reducing.
The fire chief and the council on aging director briefed the committee ahead of budget season.
Meetings were set for September 9 and September 23, with schools on the 23rd; ARPA allocation decisions are still pending.

why_it_matters: Free cash and local receipts coming in above estimates affect how much the town has available at budget time, and members questioned whether the town is effectively budgeting to create free cash.
Lower interest income and undecided ARPA allocations bear on FY22 revenue estimates, which feed the next tax levy and any money residents are asked to vote on.
watch_next: Finance Committee meetings on September 9 and September 23, with the schools on the 23rd.
The FY22 interest income estimate and decisions on how the town and county ARPA allocations are spent.
